definitions.explanation: A classical compound referring to flowers and birds as representative of the beauty of nature. A major theme in traditional East Asian art and poetry.

examples.japanese: {花鳥|かちょう}を{描|えが}いた{掛|か}け{軸|じく}。
examples.english: A hanging scroll depicting flowers and birds.

examples.japanese: {花鳥風月|かちょうふうげつ}を{愛|あい}でるのが{日本|にほん}の{伝統|でんとう}だ。
examples.english: Appreciating the beauties of nature is a Japanese tradition.

examples.japanese: この{画家|がか}は{花鳥画|かちょうが}で{知|し}られ、{繊細|せんさい}な{筆使|ふでづか}いで{多|おお}くの{傑作|けっさく}を{残|のこ}した。
examples.english: This painter was known for flower-and-bird paintings and left many masterpieces with delicate brushwork.

notes:
A classical literary compound representing the beauty of nature through its two most celebrated elements — flowers and birds.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {花鳥風月|かちょうふうげつ} (the beauties of nature — flowers, birds, wind, and moon)
- {花鳥画|かちょうが} (flower-and-bird painting)
- {花鳥|かちょう}を{愛|め}でる (appreciate flowers and birds)

{花鳥風月|かちょうふうげつ} is a well-known four-character compound (yojijukugo) meaning the beauties of nature or the elegant appreciation of natural scenery. It is used to describe a refined aesthetic sensibility. {花鳥画|かちょうが} is a major genre in East Asian painting.

Note the homophone {課長|かちょう} (section chief), which is completely different.
